foco: Falar da rotina de outra pessoa com "he", "she" e "it": afirmar, negar com "doesn't" e perguntar com "does".
conteudoAlvo: he / she / it: works, studies, watches, goes, has
She teaches English. She doesn't teach Japanese.
Does he work? Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't.
Where does she work? What time does he get up?
comoIntegrar: Compare com a Aula 23: "I live in New York." vira "He lives in New York."
Use as horas da Aula 21: "What time does your brother get up?", "He gets up at 6:00."
regrasDaAula: O verbo muda só na afirmativa: "She works.", "She doesn't work.", "Does she work?"

exemplos.enunciado: Complete com o verbo "study": "My sister ___ at home."
Passe para a negativa: "She teaches English."

limites: Dias da semana só "on Fridays" e "on Mondays": os outros vêm mais adiante.
Sem "always", "never", "How often" e sem passado: ainda não estudei.
primeiraQuestao: Vamos começar pela afirmativa. Eu digo "I work." Como fica essa frase com "he"?
resumoAutorizado: Negativa: "She doesn't teach Japanese." O verbo volta à forma-base.
Perguntas: "Does he like coffee?", "Yes, he does.", "Where does she work?"
resumoCurto: Rotina com "he", "she", "it": "works", "studies", "watches", "has"; negativa com "doesn't"; pergunta com "does".
